topic.name: Calculating Areas of Right Triangles Using Trigonometry

question.text: Given that $\tan(m\angle{A}) = \dfrac{12}{5},$ calculate the area (in square units) of $\triangle ABC$ shown above.
question.explanation:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is \[ \mathcal{A} = \dfrac12 AC \cdot BC. \]

We are given that $\tan(m\angle{A}) = \dfrac{12}5.$ Notice that relative to $\angle{A},$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overline{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overline{AC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x{:}$ \begin{align} \tan (m\angle{A}) &=\dfrac{BC}{AC} \\[5pt] \dfrac{12}{5} &=\dfrac{10x+4}{6x-2} \\[5pt] 12(6x-2) &= 5(10x+4) \\[5pt] 72x-24 &= 50x+20 \\[5pt] 22x &= 44 \\[5pt] x &= 2 \end{align}

So, the side lengths are

\begin{align*} BC &= 10x+4 = 10(2)+4=24,\\[5pt] AC &= 6x - 2 = 6(2)-2=10. \end{align*}

Therefore, the area of $\triangle{ABC}$ is \begin{align} \mathcal A & = \dfrac 1 2 AC\cdot BC \\[5pt] &= \dfrac 1 2 \cdot 10 \cdot 24 \\[5pt] &= 120. \end{align}

example.title: Finding the Area of a Triangle by Solving for a Variable Given a Trigonometric Ratio of One Angle

question.text: In square units rounded to one decimal place, find the area of $\triangle ABC$ shown above.
question.explanation:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is \[ \mathcal{A} = \dfrac12 BC \cdot AB. \]

We are given that $m\angle{A} = 30^\circ.$ Notice that relative to $\angle{A},$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overline{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overline{AB}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x{:}$

\begin{align} %\tan{A} &=\dfrac{\textrm{opposite}}{\textrm{adjacent}}\\[5pt] \tan(m\angle{A}) &=\dfrac{BC}{AB}\\[5pt] \tan (30^{\circ}) &= \dfrac{x-1}{x+2}\\[5pt] \tan (30^{\circ})(x+2) &= x-1\\[5pt] x\tan (30^{\circ}) + 2\tan (30^{\circ}) &= x-1\\[5pt] x\tan (30^{\circ}) - x &= -1-2\tan (30^{\circ}) \\[5pt] x(\tan (30^{\circ}) - 1) &= -1 - 2\tan (30^{\circ})\\[5pt] x(1 - \tan (30^{\circ})) &= 1 + 2\tan (30^{\circ})\\[5pt] x &= \dfrac{1+2\tan (30^{\circ})}{1-\tan (30^{\circ})}\\[5pt] x & = 5.098\,0\ldots \end{align}

So, the side lengths are \begin{align} BC&= x-1 = 5.098\,0 - 1 =4.098\,0\ldots,\\[5pt] AB&= x+2 = 5.098\,0 + 2 = 7.098\,0\ldots. \end{align}

Therefore, the area of $\triangle{ABC}$ is

\begin{align*} \mathcal A %& = \dfrac 1 2 \cdot BC \cdot AB\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{2}(4.098\,0\ldots) (7.098\,0\ldots) \\[5pt] & =14.543\,8\ldots\\[5pt] &\approx 14.5, \end{align*} rounded to the one decimal place.

example.title: Finding the Area of a Triangle by Solving for a Variable Given an Angle

question.text: Given that $\tan(m\angle{B}) = \dfrac{3}{2},$ the exact area of $\triangle ABC$ shown above is
question.explanation:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is \[ \mathcal{A} = \dfrac12 AC \cdot BC. \]

We are given that $\tan(m\angle{B}) = \dfrac{3}{2}.$ Notice that relative to $\angle{B},$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overline{AC}$ and adjacent side $\overline{BC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x{:}$

\begin{align} \tan (m\angle{B}) &=\dfrac{AC}{BC} \\[5pt] \dfrac{3}{2} &=\dfrac{x+3}{3x-5}\\[5pt] 3(3x-5) & =2(x+3)\\[5pt] 9x - 15 & = 2x+6\\[5pt] 7x &=21\\[5pt] x & = 3 \end{align}

So, the side lengths are \begin{align*} BC &= 3x-5 = 3(3)-5 = 4,\\[5pt] AC &= x+3 = 3+3 = 6. \end{align*}

Therefore, the area of $\triangle{ABC}$ is \begin{align} \mathcal A & = \dfrac 1 2 AC\cdot BC \\[5pt] &= \dfrac 1 2 \cdot 6 \cdot 4 \\[5pt] &=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{12}. \end{align}

example.title: Finding the Area of a Triangle by Solving for a Variable Given a Trigonometric Ratio of One Angle

question.text: Given that $\tan \theta = 3,$ the exact area of $\triangle ABC$ shown above is
question.explanation:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is \[ \mathcal{A} = \dfrac12 AC \cdot BC. \]

We are given that $\tan \theta = 3,$ where $\theta = m\angle{B}.$ Notice we're also given the length of the side $\overline{AC}$ opposite to $\angle{B}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to find the length of the adjacent side $\overline{BC}{:}$

\begin{align} \tan \theta &= \dfrac {AC}{BC} \\[5pt] 3 &= \dfrac{15}{BC} \\[5pt] BC &= \dfrac{15}{3} \\[5pt] BC &=5 \end{align}

Therefore, the area of $\triangle{ABC}$ is \begin{align} \mathcal A &= \dfrac 1 2 AC \cdot BC \\[5pt] & =\dfrac 1 2 \cdot 15 \cdot 5 \\[5pt] & = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{37.5}. \end{align}
